rationale: M37.19 (#612) store-phase. The rust grammar already distinguishes a body-bearing function from a body-less one in the NODE TYPE the walk switches on — `function_item` vs `function_signature_item` — and line 192 of real-rust-analyzer.ts handled BOTH in one branch. The distinction was used only to decide scope; nothing was published, so an `extern "C" { fn f(); }` FFI declaration emitted a `function` symbol indistinguishable from the definition that implements it in another file, and name resolution could pick the declaration. Only the published fact was missing, so the fix adds `metadata.isDeclaration` to the same createSymbol metadata the branch already builds — no new walk, no new node test. MEASURED ON THIS EXACT FILE by dumping the analyzer output through the fixture harness' own loader (wasm/tree-sitter-rust.wasm, RealRustAnalyzer): ffi_decl:16 isDeclaration=true, Runnable::sig_only:20 isDeclaration=true, body_fn:23-25 ABSENT, Runnable:19-21 ABSENT (the trait itself is not a function declaration). Two-sided on purpose: a rule that marked every function fails the `forbidSymbols` half.

expectSymbols.name: ffi_decl
expectSymbols.comment: `extern "C" { fn ffi_decl() -> i32; }` — a body-less FFI declaration. This is the shape that can compete with a definition in another file.

expectSymbols.name: sig_only
expectSymbols.comment: a trait method signature — also a `function_signature_item`, also body-less

expectSymbols.name: body_fn
expectSymbols.comment: a plain `pub fn` with a body (`function_item`)

forbidSymbols.name: body_fn
forbidSymbols.comment: NEGATIVE HALF: a `function_item` is a DEFINITION. Marking every function, or keying the flag off `isMethod`, fails this entry.

forbidSymbols.name: Runnable
forbidSymbols.comment: NEGATIVE HALF: the trait container is not a function declaration — the flag must stay on the functions.
